question: An analyst runs a research task that draws on connected internal mail and documents, then pastes large parts of the result into a public blog post. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Publishing the output automatically grants the blog's readers access to the connected data sources.
B) Research output is watermarked, so publishing any part of it identifies the analyst to everyone who reads the post.
C) Internal material reached through the connected sources can be carried straight into text meant for the public.
D) Research cannot draw on connected internal sources at all, so the analyst's result will be empty.
correct_answers: C) Internal material reached through the connected sources can be carried straight into text meant for the public.
explanations: Publishing text does not grant anyone access to the underlying systems.
There is no such identifying watermark on output.
Correct. Output built from internal sources may quote or paraphrase material that was never meant to leave the company.
Research can use connected sources, which is precisely why the output needs checking.
